title: Autoscaling dashboards (bounds + predictive) — mockup notes + alert ideas
content:
Purpose / audience
- Audience: SRE on-call + Eng Infra (debugging), Product (rollout health), and CS/TAMs (customer-facing QBR + escalations).
- This doc is the messy working companion to the more formal Confluence dashboard spec. Capture: (1) panel layout sketches in words, (2) alert ideas, (3) label/cardinality constraints, (4) what CS needs for QBRs.

Scope
- Dedicated autoscaling policy: min/max bounds + predictive scaling signals.
- Deployment-level visibility first; account-level summary second.
- Must support pilot + GA: feature-flagged deployments, multi-region.

Non-goals (for now)
- Per-request / per-trace debugging inside this dashboard (use tracing tooling).
- Cross-region placement optimization views.

Design principles (Grafana UX)
1) Start with “What is happening?” then “Why?” then “What do I do now?”
2) Everything defaults to low-cardinality views; drilldowns require explicit selection.
3) Make the bounded state obvious. Customers will latch onto: “Why didn’t you scale?”
4) Separate scaling intent vs capacity reality:
   - requested desired (what the algorithm wanted)
   - bounded desired (clamped by min/max)
   - actual provisioned (what fleet provided)
5) Explicitly show prediction quality + staleness; predictive mode will get blamed for reactive issues and vice versa.

Proposed dashboard suite (top-level navigation)
A) Dedicated Autoscaling — Overview (fleet + rollout health)
B) Dedicated Autoscaling — Deployment Drilldown (single deployment)
C) Predictive Signals — Quality & Staleness
D) Bounds — Saturation & Customer Impact (max bound hit / min unmet)
E) Events — Scale decisions + audit trail (thin view; link to logs)
F) CS/QBR — Customer-friendly weekly summary (curated)

A) Dashboard: Dedicated Autoscaling — Overview
Default variables:
- region (single select) default=all
- environment (prod/stage)
- feature_flag (bounds_enabled / predictive_enabled) (multi)
- gpu_type (optional)
- NOTE: no default customer_id variable in overview.

Panels (top to bottom):
1) Rollout coverage
- % of Dedicated deployments with bounds enabled
- % with predictive enabled
- count of deployments by region
- Panel note: include “pilot only” label to avoid confusion.

2) Fleet health at a glance (to contextualize scaling failures)
- GPU allocation pressure / shortage indicators (if available)
- Provisioning errors rate (aggregate)

3) Bound-hit rate (aggregate)
- “Max bound hit rate” (deployments experiencing clamp to max / hour)
- “Min bound unmet count” (deployments whose actual < min)
- Split by region, optionally by gpu_type (low-cardinality)

4) Queue / latency symptom tracker (aggregate)
- p95 queue depth (or queue time) across Dedicated
- p95 end-to-end latency across Dedicated
- % of traffic in deployments with sustained queueing + max clamp

5) Oscillation / churn signals
- Scale events per deployment per hour (distribution + top N)
- “Config churn” count (policy updates per deployment per day) — if emitted

Drilldown links:
- Click-through from Top N deployments (by max clamp + queue) to Deployment Drilldown.

B) Dashboard: Dedicated Autoscaling — Deployment Drilldown
Variables (explicit):
- deployment_id (required)
- region (auto from deployment, but allow override if a deployment has multi-region footprints)
- time_zone (default UTC; CS wants customer local time)

Panels:
1) “Capacity timeline” (single chart; this is the hero panel)
- Lines:
  - requested_desired_replicas
  - bounded_desired_replicas
  - actual_running_replicas
- Overlays:
  - max_bound (horizontal)
  - min_bound (horizontal)
- Annotations:
  - scale_up/down events (reason)
  - policy change events (who/what)

2) “Why are we scaling?” (signals overlay)
- Queue depth and/or queue time
- Saturation signals (GPU util / KV cache pressure / admission control) — whatever is stable
- Error rate (timeouts, 5xx)
- For predictive-enabled: predicted_demand (tokens/s or req/s), actual_demand

3) “Bounded state + impact”
- Bound clamp status (binary) time series: at_max_bound / at_min_bound
- Counter: max_bound_hit_total (delta)
- Estimated “lost capacity” when clamped (requested - bounded)
- Customer impact proxy: queue time above SLO threshold while at_max_bound

4) “Prediction quality (if predictive enabled)”
- predicted vs actual demand
- prediction error (absolute and %)
- prediction staleness age
- confidence score (if available)
- Note: show fallback-to-reactive periods (predictor stale/unavailable)

5) “Stability / oscillation”
- Scale events count (up, down) with cooldown in effect
- Average step size
- “Decision reversals” within N minutes (proxy for oscillation)

6) “Provisioning reality”
- Pending replicas (desired - running)
- Provisioning latency histogram (if available)
- Provisioning errors (quota, capacity shortage)
- Explicit callout for region shortage scenario: actual < min for > X minutes.

7) Links (bottom)
- Link to structured logs for scaling decisions (pre-filtered by deployment_id)
- Link to audit log events for policy changes
- Link to runbook section “Max bound saturation” / “Min unmet due to shortage”

C) Dashboard: Predictive Signals — Quality & Staleness
Goal: detect when predictive is making things worse and when the predictor is simply stale.

Panels:
- Predictor availability (% time predictions present)
- Staleness distribution (p50/p95 age)
- Error distribution (p50/p95) by region
- Top N deployments by persistent over-prediction (waste risk)
- Top N deployments by persistent under-prediction (latency risk)
- “Fallback rate to reactive” and reasons (stale vs null vs error)

D) Dashboard: Bounds — Saturation & Customer Impact
Goal: answer: “customers are capped; how bad is it?”

Panels:
- Deployments at max bound now (table; top N only)
- Max bound hit rate trend (by region)
- Queue time while at max bound (aggregate + per top N)
- Deployments with min unmet (table)
- Min unmet duration (heatmap)
- Correlation: max clamp + p95 latency regressions

E) Dashboard: Events — Scale decisions + audit trail (thin)
- Timeline of scale decisions (reason codes)
- Timeline of policy updates (who initiated, API vs Console vs Terraform)
- Note: keep this light; heavy event exploration should live in logs/audit tooling.

F) Dashboard: CS/QBR — Customer-friendly weekly summary
CS/TAM feedback (Rachel + Liam): QBRs need a ‘story’ slide, not raw timeseries.

Proposed output sections (each panel should be exportable as an image or CSV):
1) “Reliability & performance” (last 7/30 days)
- p95 latency (customer deployment)
- % time meeting latency SLO
- incidents / notable events (manual annotation support would help)

2) “Capacity behavior”
- Average running replicas (or GPU-hours) and range
- Peak usage window (day-of-week/time-of-day) — time zone aware
- Scale-up lead time vs ramps (if predictive enabled)

3) “Bounds effectiveness”
- Max bound hit: hours capped + top capped intervals
- If capped, show “impact”: queue time above threshold while capped
- Min bound: hours below min (should be ~0; if not, call out shortage)

4) “Prediction summary (if enabled)”
- Prediction error p50/p95
- Fallback-to-reactive frequency
- Recommended tuning notes (cooldown/bounds suggestions) — optional, can be manual playbook-driven

5) “Action items” (CS template)
- Proposed config changes (min/max, predictive toggle)
- Next check-in date

High-cardinality / metric label notes (IMPORTANT)
We need to stay within Prometheus/Grafana sanity limits and avoid exploding series.

Guidelines:
- Allowed labels on most time series:
  - region
  - deployment_id (only when explicitly selecting a deployment; avoid aggregations across all deployment_id)
  - policy_mode (reactive/predictive)
  - reason_code (small bounded enum)
  - gpu_type (small enum)
- Avoid / do NOT include as labels:
  - customer_id on high-volume counters/histograms (unless we can guarantee bounded cardinality and/or separate metrics store)
  - request_id / trace_id / model_version (unless very low cardinality)
  - free-form strings (error messages)

Implementation pattern in Grafana:
- Overview dashboards use aggregate metrics WITHOUT deployment_id label.
- Drilldown dashboards query metrics WITH deployment_id after variable selection.
- Top N tables: use recording rules to precompute “top capped deployments” per region to avoid ad-hoc heavy queries.

CS requirement tension:
- CS wants “customer name” filters. Do NOT label metrics with customer_name.
- Proposal: Grafana variable backed by a small lookup table (deployment_id -> account_display_name) sourced from control-plane inventory, NOT embedded as metric labels.
- If we can’t integrate a lookup quickly: provide a lightweight internal tool or a static mapping for pilot accounts.

Alert ideas (first pass)
We should page on customer-impacting conditions and ticket on informational conditions.

Paging candidates (SRE on-call):
1) Max bound saturation + sustained queue buildup (customer-impact)
- Condition:
  - at_max_bound == 1 for > 10m
  AND queue_time_p95 > threshold (or queue_depth > threshold) for > 10m
  AND traffic_rate > minimum (avoid paging on idle deployments)
- Route: Dedicated on-call (eng-sre) + notify CS for pilot accounts.
- Add runbook link: “Max bound saturation (customer capped)”

2) Min bound unmet (capacity shortage / provisioning failure)
- Condition:
  - actual_running_replicas < min_bound for > 10m
- Add label: shortage_reason_code if we have it (quota/capacity/provision_error)
- Route: Infra on-call; also create customer-visible status note (CS comms) if sustained.

3) Predictor stale/unavailable while predictive enabled (degrades behavior)
- Condition:
  - predictive_enabled == 1
  AND prediction_staleness_age_seconds > 900 (15m)
  OR predictor_error_rate > threshold
- Route: ticket (non-page) unless correlated with queueing/latency. For pilot, maybe page during canary windows.

Ticket-only (non-page) alerts:
4) Oscillation / too many scale events
- Condition: scale_events_per_hour > X for N hours
- Use to detect cooldown/guardrail tuning issues.

5) Frequent config churn
- Condition: policy_updates_per_day > X
- Likely indicates customer automation gone wild or Terraform loop; CS follow-up.

6) Bound hit rate trending up (early warning)
- Condition: max_bound_hit_rate increasing week-over-week
- Useful for capacity planning + upsell Dedicated commits.

Alert noise control / suppression
- Require sustained duration windows; avoid single spikes.
- Suppress during known maintenance windows (flagged by infra events feed, if available).
- Pilot accounts: route extra notifications to #support or TAM channel but avoid paging entire org.

Notes from CS/TAM (Rachel, Dev, Liam)
- During escalations, customers ask 3 questions:
  1) Did Redwood try to scale and get blocked by the max I set?
  2) If yes, what was the impact (queue/latency) and for how long?
  3) If no, why didn’t Redwood scale earlier (predictor wrong vs cooldown vs signals)?
- QBR needs:
  - “Hours capped at max bound” and “peak demand window” as a simple slide.
  - Any “min unmet” should be called out as exceptional and paired with remediation + comms template.
  - Time zone alignment: show charts in customer local time; avoid confusion around daily ramps.

Open questions / TODOs
- Metric definitions: confirm exact metric names + reason_code enums with Logan + Vanessa (align with naming standards doc).
- Queue depth vs queue time: runtime team flagged queue depth instability for some models; prefer queue time if available (needs confirmation from Keiko).
- Demand unit: tokens/sec vs requests/sec. Predictive service likely outputs req/sec; autoscaler uses effective capacity in tokens/sec. Need a consistent mapping for charting.
- Inventory lookup: how do we map deployment_id -> account_display_name in Grafana safely? (Control plane API? nightly export?)
- Do we need a separate “exec view” panel for rollout health (Priya asked for a single screenshot for GA go/no-go).

Next steps
- Sergio: rough Grafana dashboard draft in dev folder (2–3 panels per dashboard) using stub metric names; validate layout.
- Allison: sync with Aisha (SLOs) on which alerts are page vs ticket.
- Rachel/Dev: provide 2–3 anonymized QBR examples so we can tune the CS/QBR dashboard to match real customer expectations.
- After first draft: run a quick cardinality audit against pilot traffic before enabling wide-access.
